name: Monte Carlo
notes: Single source. Every one of the 79 devices comes from the IC parts list in TM-149, and that is the only printing of this manual in the corpus that carries the list. No component-location drawing has been read. Nothing here has been checked against a second source, which is the test every other board on this site has passed, and the board page says so.

The grid spacing is nominal — the designators are what the parts list gives, but nothing has measured the board. Rows run R to A and columns 1 to 10; the row span is the standard Atari alphabet between the outermost letters seen, so rows with no device on them are still drawn as positions the board has.
conflicts: 4 device name(s) could not be recovered and are not placed: C3 (7437), E2 (8304B), J6 (8304B), K4 (8304B). Each is an OCR of a part number whose function number does not name anything the packaging table knows, and with only one printing there is no second reading to repair it from.

Devices withdrawn 2026-09-02. These cells were claimed twice by the same parts list, and merge_ic_locations took whichever reading came last — locations() detected the collision and returned it, but harvest() discarded that half of the answer. So each of these was one of two readings picked by position in the file rather than by evidence. They are off the map until something settles them. The withdrawn readings are kept here because a repairer at the bench is better served by 'it is one of these two' than by silence: B1 (74LS241/74LS244); A6 (74LS273/74LS374); P7 (74LS273/74LS374); H8 (74LS273/74LS374).
